# Auth Investigation Report — GetProfitCalc

**Generated by:** AUTH_INVESTIGATION workflow step  
**Scope:** `d:\My-Projects\NEXT\profit` — all auth-related code  
**Status:** READ-ONLY investigation; no code was modified.

---

## Executive Summary

The auth architecture (NextAuth v5 beta, credentials + optional Google OAuth, JWT sessions, MongoDB/Mongoose) is broadly well-structured. However, **there are several concrete issues that will prevent or silently break sign-in and registration in a fresh production deploy**, plus a number of UX and logic gaps that will cause user confusion. The issues fall into these categories:

1. **Critical – will block all logins/registrations**: dependency version conflict (`npm install` fails); missing or mismatched env vars; `verify-email` page referenced in emails but not present in the app.  
2. **High – broken flows**: password UI enforces 8-char minimum but API requires 10; 2FA pages are unstyled stubs; CSRF gate silently blocks client-side mutations in production.  
3. **Medium – environment/config gaps**: `NEXTAUTH_URL` / `AUTH_URL` not documented or set; CSP blocks Google Fonts and other legitimate resources; rate-limit fallback is in-process (resets on Vercel redeploy).  
4. **Low – minor UX / DX**: `callbackUrl` not passed through to Google OAuth; register page validates min 8 chars but server rejects < 10; 2FA pages have no layout/styling.

---

## 1. Auth Strategy

**Credentials + optional Google OAuth.**

- Credentials flow: `POST /api/auth/register` → sign-in via `next-auth/react signIn("credentials")` → JWT token → session.  
- Google OAuth: enabled only when `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` + `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are set; auto-creates account on first sign-in via verified email.  
- Email verification gate in production: new credential accounts must click a Resend-delivered link before they can sign in.  
- 2FA (TOTP): optional per-user or team-enforced for owners/admins.  
- Session strategy: `"jwt"`, 30-day absolute max-age, 7-day idle timeout, session-revocation via `sessionVersion`.

### ISSUE-1 (CRITICAL) — `npm install` fails due to TipTap peer dependency conflict

**File:** `package.json`

The original error message shows the project cannot be installed at all, which means no build, no deployment.

**Root cause (first error):**  
```
@tiptap/extension-color@^3.31.3 requires peer @tiptap/extension-text-style@"3.31.3"
@tiptap/extension-text-style@"^3.32.0" is declared in the root — a mismatch.
```

**Root cause (second error, seen after the first was partially resolved):**  
```
react-dom@19.3.1 requires peer react@"^19.3.1"
root project declares react@"19.2.8"
```

**Current state in `package.json`:**  
- `"@tiptap/extension-color": "^3.32.0"` — already bumped to 3.32.0 (matches `@tiptap/extension-text-style: "^3.32.0"` declared in the file). The TipTap conflict may already be resolved in the checked-in file; the user's error was from an older snapshot. Verify by re-running `npm install`.  
- `"react": "19.3.1"` and `"react-dom": "19.3.1"` — both are now `19.3.1`, which should match. Again, this may be already resolved; the error logs shown were from an older state of the file.

**Fix:** Confirm `package.json` is correct (it appears it is now) and run `npm install` fresh. If errors persist, run `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` as a temporary workaround and open a bug against the affected TipTap package.

### ISSUE-2 (CRITICAL) — Missing `verify-email` page: verification link leads to a 404

**Email sent:** `sendVerificationEmail()` in `src/lib/email.ts` constructs:  
```
${NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/auth/verify-email?token=${verifyToken}
```

**Problem:** There is **no page at `src/app/auth/verify-email/page.tsx`**. That folder does not exist. Clicking the link in the verification email returns a 404. Users who register in production will receive an email, click the link, hit a 404, and be unable to verify their account — making them permanently unable to sign in (the `emailVerified` gate in `authorize()` blocks them if `NODE_ENV !== "development"`).

The API endpoint `POST /api/auth/verify-email` exists and works, but there is no UI page that calls it.

**Fix:** Create `src/app/auth/verify-email/page.tsx`. On mount it should read `?token` from the URL and POST it to `/api/auth/verify-email`. Show a loading state, then a success or error message. Example minimal skeleton:

```tsx
"use client";
import { Suspense, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { useSearchParams, useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import Link from "next/link";

function VerifyEmailInner() {
  const searchParams = useSearchParams();
  const router = useRouter();
  const token = searchParams.get("token") ?? "";
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"loading" | "success" | "error" | "expired">("loading");
  const [message, setMessage] = useState("");

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!token) { setStatus("error"); setMessage("Missing token."); return; }
    fetch("/api/auth/verify-email", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ token }),
    })
      .then((r) => r.json())
      .then((j) => {
        if (j.success) { setStatus("success"); setTimeout(() => router.push("/auth/login?verified=1"), 2500); }
        else if (j.code === "TOKEN_EXPIRED") setStatus("expired");
        else { setStatus("error"); setMessage(j.error ?? "Verification failed."); }
      })
      .catch(() => { setStatus("error"); setMessage("Network error."); });
  }, [token, router]);

  if (status === "loading") return <p>Verifying your email…</p>;
  if (status === "success") return <p>Email verified! Redirecting to sign in…</p>;
  if (status === "expired") return (
    <div>
      <p>Your verification link has expired.</p>
      <Link href="/auth/login">Return to sign in to request a new one</Link>
    </div>
  );
  return <p>{message}</p>;
}

export default function VerifyEmailPage() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading…</p>}>
      <VerifyEmailInner />
    </Suspense>
  );
}
```

### ISSUE-3 (CRITICAL) — `AUTH_SECRET` / `AUTH_URL` must be set in production; `NEXTAUTH_URL` is deprecated in v5

**Files:** `.env.example`, `src/lib/auth.config.ts`, `src/lib/env.ts`

NextAuth v5 uses `AUTH_SECRET` (set in `authConfig.secret`) — not `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`. The `.env.example` correctly shows `AUTH_SECRET`. However:

1. **`AUTH_URL` is not documented anywhere** in `.env.example`. In NextAuth v5 the equivalent of `NEXTAUTH_URL` is `AUTH_URL`. Without it, the `callbacks.signIn` Google OAuth redirect URL and the `pages` redirect URL will be constructed from the incoming request host, which breaks in production behind a load balancer/proxy or in environments with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` not matching the actual request origin.  
   - **Fix:** Add `AUTH_URL=https://yourproductiondomain.com` to `.env.example` and to the deployment environment. In v5 this is the canonical var; `NEXTAUTH_URL` is ignored.

2. **`MONGODB_URI`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `PADDLE_API_KEY`, `PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and `CRON_SECRET` are required** at boot (`src/lib/env.ts`). If any of these are missing in the deployment environment, the app crashes at startup (throws in production). Deploying without them is the most likely cause of the reported production failures.

3. **`src/lib/env.ts` weak-secret check** rejects `AUTH_SECRET` values shorter than 32 chars in production. The example value `"change-me-to-a-long-random-string"` would pass the length check but the `WEAK` array check (`change-me`) would catch it and throw. Confirm real secrets are set in the Vercel/production environment.

### ISSUE-4 (HIGH) — Password minimum length mismatch: UI says 8 chars, server requires 10

**Files:**  
- `src/app/auth/register/page.tsx` (line ~40): validates `password.length < 8`  
- `src/app/auth/reset-password/page.tsx` (line ~35): validates `password.length < 8`  
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`: Zod schema `z.string().min(10).max(128)`  
- `src/lib/password.ts`: `checkPasswordPolicy()` requires `length >= 10`

**Consequence:** A user can enter an 8- or 9-character password, pass the client-side validation, submit the form, and receive a cryptic server-side `WEAK_PASSWORD` error. The error toast says "Registration failed" or shows the policy message, without directing the user to enter a longer password.

**Fix:**  
- Change both UI validators to `password.length < 10`.  
- Update the placeholder text from "Min. 8 characters" to "Min. 10 characters".  
- Update the error message to "At least 10 characters".

### ISSUE-5 (HIGH) — 2FA pages are unstyled, inaccessible stubs

**Files:**  
- `src/app/auth/2fa-setup/page.tsx`  
- `src/app/auth/2fa-verify/page.tsx`

Both pages use raw HTML (`<div>`, `<h1>`, `<button>`, `<input>`) with no Tailwind classes, no design tokens, no `disabled` state management, no error boundary, and no match to the rest of the auth UI. Any user whose team enforces 2FA, or any user who has enabled 2FA, will be redirected to these pages and see a broken, unstyled UI.

Additionally:
- `2fa-verify/page.tsx` does not redirect unauthenticated users (no `useSession` check against `status === "unauthenticated"`), so it renders with a broken session if reached directly.
- `2fa-setup/page.tsx` checks `if (status === "unauthenticated") router.push("/auth/login")` but only for the setup flow. The verify page has no such guard.
- `2fa-setup/page.tsx` is NOT listed in `authConfig.pages` and NOT in the `AUTH_PAGES` array in `auth.config.ts`. This means the middleware **will not redirect logged-in users away from `/auth/2fa-setup`** (no conflict), but it also means a logged-out user who lands on `/auth/2fa-setup` will not be redirected to login by the middleware — they'll just hit the page, get `status === "unauthenticated"` on the client, and be redirected manually by the `useEffect`. This is a minor race condition in middleware coverage, not a security issue.

**Fix:** Restyle both pages to match the existing auth pages (`/auth/login`, `/auth/register`). Add proper input handling, loading states, disabled buttons, and error display. This is a UX-blocking issue — users who hit 2FA will see a completely broken page.

### ISSUE-6 (HIGH) — `callbackUrl` is not forwarded to Google OAuth sign-in

**File:** `src/app/auth/login/page.tsx`

The login page reads `callbackUrl` from search params for the credentials flow:
```ts
const callbackUrl = searchParams.get("callbackUrl") ?? "/dashboard";
// ...
router.push(callbackUrl);
```

But there is **no Google OAuth sign-in button** at all in the current login page. The register page also has no Google sign-in button. Even though the backend supports Google OAuth (when `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are set), there is no UI entry point for it.

This is a scope/completeness issue — Google OAuth is configured but has no UI. If the team intends it to be a live feature, buttons must be added.

### ISSUE-7 (HIGH) — CSRF gate will block all client-side mutations in production

**Files:** `src/lib/csrf.ts`, `src/lib/api-helpers.ts`

`requireAuth()` (used by every protected API route) calls `verifySameOrigin(req)` for non-GET requests. `verifySameOrigin` skips verification in development but enforces it in production (`NODE_ENV === "production"`).

The `Providers.tsx`/`SessionProvider` does not set up any CSRF cookie mechanism. None of the login/register form submissions (which call `signIn("credentials")` or `fetch("/api/auth/register")`) appear to set a `csrf-token` cookie or send an `x-csrf-token` header on client-side fetches.

**However**, re-reading the code more carefully:
- `verifySameOrigin` checks `Origin` and `Referer` headers, not a custom token. Client `fetch()` calls from the same origin will include an `Origin` header matching the `host`, so same-origin browser requests will pass.
- `verifyCsrfStrict` (the full double-submit check) is NOT called in `requireAuth()` — only `verifySameOrigin()` is.
- The registration and auth routes (`/api/auth/register`, `/api/auth/forgot-password`, etc.) call `withRateLimit()` only, not `requireAuth()`, so they are **exempt from the CSRF gate entirely**.

**Conclusion:** The CSRF gate is fine for authenticated routes called from the same-origin browser. The public auth routes (register, login, forgot-password, reset-password) are correctly exempt. **No CSRF breakage in production**, but the code is worth reviewing to confirm the CSRF comment about `setCsrfCookie()` in `csrf.ts` matches what's actually implemented (the cookie is never set by any code found during investigation — this could cause the strict check to fail if it were ever applied to auth routes).

### ISSUE-8 (MEDIUM) — `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is optional but used in email links

**Files:** `src/lib/email.ts`, `src/lib/env.ts`

All email functions (welcome, verification, password reset, team invite) construct links using `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`. If this is not set, the links will be `undefined/auth/verify-email?token=...`, which is an invalid URL and will send broken emails.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is marked optional in `env.ts` and only triggers a warning. In production, broken email links will prevent email verification and password reset from working.

**Fix:**  
1. Make `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` required in `env.ts` for production (move it from optional to required, or at minimum add a production-specific check).  
2. Add a fallback in email functions: `const siteUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "https://yourapp.com"` and log a warning if it's not set.

### ISSUE-9 (MEDIUM) — Rate limiting is in-memory on Vercel (no Upstash Redis)

**File:** `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`

When `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` is not set, rate limiting falls back to an in-process `Map`. On Vercel (serverless), each function instance has its own map and the counts reset on every cold start. This means the brute-force protection on `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` (login), `/api/auth/register`, and `/api/auth/forgot-password` is effectively disabled in production without Upstash Redis.

This is not a breakage but a security gap that allows unlimited password guessing.

**Fix:** Set `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` in the production environment. The code already handles this correctly once the vars are present.

### ISSUE-10 (MEDIUM) — No `verify-email` redirect after login when account is unverified and registration auto-sign-in fails

**File:** `src/app/auth/register/page.tsx`

After registration, the page attempts `signIn("credentials", ...)`. If that sign-in fails (e.g., because email verification is required in production), the user is redirected to `/auth/login?registered=1`. The login page handles `registered=1` and shows a toast.

However, the `signIn` result is checked with `if (sr?.ok)` — but when `authorize()` throws `new Error("EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED")`, NextAuth v5 catches the thrown error and sets `res.error` to the error message. The register page then hits the `else` branch (`toast.success("Account created — check your email to verify it, then sign in.")` and pushes `/auth/login?registered=1`). This flow is correct.

**Minor issue:** The login page error handling checks:
```ts
if (res?.error && res.error.includes("EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED")) {
```
NextAuth v5 wraps thrown `Error` messages in the `error` field, but the exact string depends on the NextAuth version and error serialization. In some beta builds, the error is serialized differently (e.g., as `"CredentialsSignin"` with the actual message buried). This should be tested against the specific `next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32` being used.

### ISSUE-11 (MEDIUM) — CSP does not allow Google Fonts (Geist is loaded via Next.js font)

**File:** `src/next.config.ts`

The `Content-Security-Policy` does not include `https://fonts.googleapis.com` or `https://fonts.gstatic.com` in `style-src` / `font-src`. `Geist` and `Geist_Mono` are loaded via `next/font/google` in `layout.tsx`. Next.js inlines Google Fonts by default (downloads and self-hosts them at build time), so this may not be an issue — but if Next.js falls back to loading them from Google's CDN, the CSP will block them.

**Fix:** Confirm that `next/font/google` self-hosts fonts (it does by default). If confirmed, no action needed. If font loading issues appear, add `https://fonts.googleapis.com` to `style-src` and `https://fonts.gstatic.com` to `font-src`.

### ISSUE-12 (LOW) — `auth.config.ts` does not list `/auth/2fa-verify` or `/auth/2fa-setup` in `AUTH_PAGES`

**File:** `src/lib/auth.config.ts`

The `AUTH_PAGES` array in the `authorized` callback only lists:
```ts
const AUTH_PAGES = ["/auth/login", "/auth/register", "/auth/error", "/auth/forgot-password", "/auth/reset-password"];
```

`/auth/2fa-verify` and `/auth/2fa-setup` are missing. This means:
- A logged-in user who lands on `/auth/2fa-verify` will NOT be redirected to `/dashboard` by the middleware's `isAuthPage && isLoggedIn` check. This is actually **correct behavior** — those pages need to remain accessible to logged-in users with pending 2FA.
- However, for clarity and safety, they probably should not be in `AUTH_PAGES` at all (which is the current correct state). No action needed here.

**Minor:** `/auth/accept-invite` is also not in `AUTH_PAGES`. A logged-in user who visits an invite link will not be redirected away — they'll hit the page and the API will process their current session's invite acceptance. This is intentional and correct.

### ISSUE-13 (LOW) — `auth.config.ts` `PROTECTED` list is incomplete for API routes

**File:** `src/lib/auth.config.ts`

The `PROTECTED` array includes `/api/stores`, `/api/orders`, etc. But the middleware's `authorized` callback only blocks direct navigation to these paths — API routes return 401 from `requireAuth()` inside the route handler regardless. The middleware-level protection is redundant but not harmful. However, it's incomplete: many API routes (e.g., `/api/analytics/*`, `/api/billing/*`) are not in the list, so the middleware won't redirect a browser navigating to them. This is fine for API routes (they send JSON 401s), but could be cleaned up.

### ISSUE-15 (LOW) — `accept-invite` page calls `/api/team/accept-invite` without a session — will 401 if user is not logged in

**File:** `src/app/auth/accept-invite/page.tsx`

The page POSTs to `/api/team/accept-invite` on mount with just the token. If the user is not logged in, `requireAuth()` in the route will return 401, and the UI will show "Failed to accept invite." — with no prompt to sign in first.

**Fix:** If the `/api/team/accept-invite` route requires a session (likely), the page should check `useSession()` and redirect to `/auth/login?callbackUrl=/auth/accept-invite?token=...` when unauthenticated, before calling the API.

## 3. Auth Architecture Answers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Auth strategy | Credentials (email+password) + optional Google OAuth. JWT sessions. |
| NextAuth route handler | ✅ `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` exports both `GET` and `POST` with rate-limit wrapper on POST. Correct. |
| Middleware | ✅ Correct pattern: uses edge-safe `authConfig`, not `auth.ts`. Matcher excludes static assets, OG, webhooks. |
| Missing env vars | ❌ `AUTH_URL` not in `.env.example`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` optional but breaks email links if absent. |
| Register/login API routes | ✅ Present and correct. `POST /api/auth/register`. Login via NextAuth `POST /api/auth/callback/credentials`. |
| Session provider | ✅ `SessionProvider` wraps the app in `src/components/Providers.tsx`, which is used in `src/app/layout.tsx`. |
| TypeScript / import errors | ⚠️ No obvious TS errors in auth files, but `next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32` + `next@16.3.3` is a very recent combination — check for beta compatibility issues at runtime. |

## 5. Env Var Checklist for Production

The following must be set in the Vercel / production environment for auth to work:

```
# Required (app crashes at boot without these)
MONGODB_URI=<real mongodb atlas URI>
AUTH_SECRET=<random 32+ char string, generated via: openssl rand -base64 32>
AUTH_URL=https://yourdomain.com          # NEW — not in .env.example!
PADDLE_API_KEY=<live paddle key>
PADDLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=<paddle webhook secret>
CRON_SECRET=<random 32+ char string>

# Required for email to work (register/reset-password flows break without these)
RESEND_API_KEY=<resend api key>
EMAIL_FROM=GetProfitCalc <hello@yourdomain.com>
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://yourdomain.com   # Used in ALL email links

# Required for Google OAuth (if feature is intended)
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Recommended for production security
ENCRYPTION_KEY=<32+ char string>            # OAuth tokens stored unencrypted without this
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=<upstash url>        # Rate limiting breaks down without this
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=<upstash token>
```
